# v1.9.1 — Stop the queue from walking your whole music library every download

A focused performance-and-correctness hotfix landing four bugs the v1.8.x activity-log analysis surfaced. Anyone on v1.8.x or v1.9.0 who has more than a handful of album folders under their output path — especially on artist URLs — should upgrade. We've measured 5-25× speed-ups per item on a 484-album library.

## What's fixed

- **Companion lyrics conversion no longer walks the entire output library when album hints are missing (#839).** When MeedyaDL's early Apple Music API fetch returned an empty or missing artist/album name, the companion task's lyrics conversion fell through to `find_dirs_with_ttml(output_dir)` — which on a 484-album library meant 25+ minutes per item of TTML→LRC/SRT/VTT/ASS re-conversion across every album folder you've ever downloaded. Two contributing patterns are now closed: (1) `Some("")` empty-string hints are treated the same as `None` rather than joining as `base.join("").join("") = base`, and (2) the recursive-walk-over-`base` fallback is removed entirely. When a specific album dir can't be resolved we now skip that item's companion lyrics conversion instead of converting the whole library.
- **Enrichment passes now scope to a single album dir on artist URLs (#842).** Same structural issue as #839 but affecting metadata tagging, AcoustID fingerprinting, ReplayGain analysis, and the lyrics-fallback scan. A 3-track Forrest Frank artist URL on the same 484-album library used to tag 69 files, fingerprint 69 files, ReplayGain-analyse 73 files, and lyrics-fallback-scan 73 tracks before any enrichment landed — turning a 30-second pass into a 6-minute walk. The enrichment task now resolves a specific album dir via `find_album_directory` at init (using artist/album hints when available, falling back to the depth-10 most-recently-modified-leaf scan from #844 when they're not) and every downstream service operates inside that scope.
- **Companion lyrics conversion runs once per item, not once per successful tier (#843).** For items where multiple companion tiers produced files (e.g. Atmos tier 2 + AAC-Legacy tier 4 both succeeding), the lyrics conversion fired inside the per-tier success branch and re-walked the same album once per tier. The Sam Rivera item the user reported burnt ~50 minutes re-converting the same TTML files twice. TTML files don't change between tiers (companions inherit them from the primary download), so the call is hoisted to once-after-the-tier-loop and gated on a new `any_tier_produced_files` flag.
- **Fast hint-recovery scan on big libraries (#844).** The fallback resolver `find_deepest_audio_dir` used for hint-less items was an *unbounded* recursive walk. On a 484-album library it added 30-60 seconds of pure I/O before any enrichment work began, limiting the practical win from #839/#842. Capped at depth 10 — the same convention `find_dirs_with_ttml` and `scan_folder_for_manifests` already use. User libraries naturally fit within 3 levels (`Music/Artist/Album/`), so 10 is generous headroom for unusual layouts.

## Notes

- **No new tests** — these are surgical changes to existing helpers that already have coverage. All 1,184 existing tests still pass on Rust 1.93 (local) and 1.95 (CI).
- **Cumulative impact for the user who reported the bug**: on a multi-tier artist-URL queue, total time per item drops from 25-50 minutes to 30-60 seconds. The 484-album walk no longer happens at all.
- **Sibling cosmetic fix #840 (multi-line dedup-URL log) already shipped in v1.9.0** alongside this group's investigation. Two more cleanups (#845 line-breaks for the `Nothing queued for` log; #846 watchdog progress signal from activity events) are tracked for the next release.
